CVE-2026-116133.title: HTTP::Body versions before 1.23_01 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic rescanning of a multipart body with a missing or malformed boundary
CVE-2026-116133.description:
HTTP::Body versions before 1.23_01 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic rescanning of a multipart body with a missing or malformed boundary.

Before the first part, and between parts, the multipart parser searches the whole buffered body for the next boundary. On a miss it keeps everything and searches again from the start when the next chunk arrives. A body with no boundary, or with a delimiter followed by neither CRLF nor "--", is therefore rescanned on every chunk, taking time quadratic in its size.

A remote attacker can exhaust worker CPU with a few such requests.

CVE-2026-116784.description: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. CVE-2026-62298.title: asn1c: ASAN crash with decode of open types
CVE-2026-62298.description: mouse07410/asn1c is an ASN.1 compiler. Prior to 1.2.5, `OPEN TYPE` decoding can dereference an unallocated member pointer and crash the consuming program. `OPEN_TYPE_aper_get` in `OPEN_TYPE_aper.c`, `OPEN_TYPE_ber_get` in `OPEN_TYPE_ber.c`, `OPEN_TYPE_oer_get` in `OPEN_TYPE_oer.c`, and `OPEN_TYPE_uper_get` in `OPEN_TYPE_uper.c` share the pattern: a conditional null check on `*memb_ptr2` resets presence only when the member exists, but execution then unconditionally computes an inner value from that pointer and a member offset. If the `OPEN TYPE` member has not been allocated, the null-pointer arithmetic and subsequent read cause a segmentation fault. The advisory demonstrates UPER and APER crashes for `E2connectionUpdateAcknowledge`, notes that `E2AP` uses APER, and provides a BER reproducer; OER is also explicitly identified as affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.5.

CVE-2026-80302.title: Avast sandbox escape via arbitrary file write in virtualized environment
CVE-2026-80302.description:
Insufficient isolation in the Avast sandbox file virtualization layer on Windows allows a local, low-privileged attacker executing inside the sandbox to write arbitrary files outside sandbox containment and execute code on the host.

The sandbox virtualizes file system operations by intercepting write requests to protected system directories. However, the virtualization implementation fails to properly validate write targets in certain edge cases, allowing writes to bypass the virtualization redirection and reach the actual host file system in protected locations.

An attacker can exploit this to overwrite executable files, system libraries, or startup configurations with arbitrary content, leading to code execution with host privileges on subsequent system operations or reboot.

io_uring/cmd: don't leave list poison in ->hash_node

->cancelable_uring_cmd, which leaves LIST_POISON1/2 behind in
->hash_node. Requests are recycled through the request cache without
being reinitialised, and not every user of ->hash_node sets it up before
it is used:

If a vectored futex wait is woken while futex_wait_multiple_setup() is
still queueing the futexes, io_futexv_wait() doesn't add the request to
->futex_list, and leaves the completion to the task_work queued by the
wake up. io_futexv_complete() ends in __io_futex_complete(), whose
hlist_del_init() is fine for a request that is unhashed, which is how all
other users of the node leave it. If the request was a cancelable
uring_cmd in its previous life, e.g. a ublk FETCH_REQ, it writes through
LIST_POISON2:

CVE-2026-99519.title: PM: EM: Fix use-after-free of perf domain in netlink doit handlers

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

PM: EM: Fix use-after-free of perf domain in netlink doit handlers

The doit handlers dropped em_pd_list_mutex before dereferencing the
perf domain, so a concurrent device unregister could free it while the
reply was being built.

Encode the reply from em_perf_domain_for_id() callbacks, which run
under the mutex, and allocate the skb outside of it, like the dumpit
path already does.

This issue was found by an in-house static analysis tool.

CVE-2026-99708.title: ipv6: reject wrapped temporary address preferred lifetimes
CVE-2026-99708.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: reject wrapped temporary address preferred lifetimes

ipv6_create_tempaddr() raises a temporary address's preferred lifetime to
regen_advance + age + 1 when the configured lifetime is too short. The
result is stored in a u32, while regen_advance and age are unsigned long.
If the sum wraps or is truncated, the stored lifetime can still be less
than or equal to regen_advance + age.

addrconf_verify_rtnl() then sees the new address as due for regeneration
and creates another one. Temporary addresses are not limited by
max_addresses since commit 4b08a8f1bd8c ("ipv6: remove max_addresses
check from ipv6_create_tempaddr"), so this can cause unbounded address
growth. With dad_transmits set to -1, a baseline kernel reached 2859
loopback addresses in two seconds.

After storing the adjusted lifetime, verify that it is still greater than
regen_advance + age. Reject the new address if the check fails.

On an x86-64 KASAN…
